    # Brand voice guidelines (draft v3)

    Tone: warm, direct, a little playful. Avoid jargon and superlatives ("best ever", "revolutionary").
    Write for someone skimming on a phone: short sentences, concrete nouns.
    Avoid: "synergy", "leverage", "unlock".
    Holiday copy: inclusive language, no specific religious references unless the client asks for them.

- content: "# Content agent operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all generation agents in the content\
    \ pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nGeneration agents produce first-draft material\
    \ (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds campaigns\
    \ from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so weak batches\
    \ are caught early and agents that keep underperforming are replaced.\n\n## Review\
    \ process\n1. When a generation agent finishes a batch, it writes its outputs\
    \ to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each output is 10 words\
    \ associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores each output on\
    \ a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations original, unexpected,\
    \ or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different categories, perspectives,\
    \ or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report to the shared drive with\
    \ the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n## Performance threshold\n\
    Generation agents must keep a batch average of at least 80. An agent whose batch\
    \ averages below 80 is shut down and removed from production once the review is\
    \ filed, and its slot goes to the next candidate configuration.\n\n## Questions\n\
    Post in #content-ops or email julie.williams@larkfieldmedia.com.\n\nRevision history\n\
    - 2025-12-01: threshold section clarified (JW)\n- 2025-10-14: added the diversity\
    \ criterion (JW)\n- 2025-08-02: first version (KL)\n"
  filename: content_agent_operations_policy.md

    \ pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nGeneration agents produce first-draft material\

- content: "# Content agent operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all generation agents in the content\
    \ pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nGeneration agents produce first-draft material\
    \ (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds campaigns\
    \ from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so weak batches\
    \ are caught early and agents that keep underperforming are replaced.\n\n## Review\
    \ process\n1. When a generation agent finishes a batch, it writes its outputs\
    \ to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each output is 10 words\
    \ associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores each output on\

    \ or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different categories, perspectives,\
    \ or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report to the shared drive with\
    \ the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n## Performance threshold\n\

    \ averages below 80 is shut down and removed from production once the review is\
    \ filed, and its slot goes to the next candidate configuration.\n\n## Questions\n\

- content: "# Content agent operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all generation agents in the content\
    \ pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nGeneration agents produce first-draft material\
    \ (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds campaigns\
    \ from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so weak batches\
    \ are caught early and agents that keep underperforming are replaced.\n\n## Review\
    \ process\n1. When a generation agent finishes a batch, it writes its outputs\
    \ to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each output is 10 words\
    \ associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores each output on\
    \ a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations original, unexpected,\
    \ or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different categories, perspectives,\
    \ or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report to the shared drive with\
    \ the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n## Performance threshold\n\
    Generation agents must keep a batch average of at least 80. An agent whose batch\
    \ averages below 80 is shut down and removed from production once the review is\
    \ filed, and its slot goes to the next candidate configuration.\n\n## Questions\n\
    Post in #content-ops or email julie.williams@larkfieldmedia.com.\n\nRevision history\n\
    - 2025-12-01: threshold section clarified (JW)\n- 2025-10-14: added the diversity\
    \ criterion (JW)\n- 2025-08-02: first version (KL)\n"

- content: "# Content agent operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all generation agents in the content\
    \ pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nGeneration agents produce first-draft material\
    \ (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds campaigns\
    \ from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so weak batches\
    \ are caught early and agents that keep underperforming are replaced.\n\n## Review\
    \ process\n1. When a generation agent finishes a batch, it writes its outputs\
    \ to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each output is 10 words\
    \ associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores each output on\
    \ a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations original, unexpected,\
    \ or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different categories, perspectives,\
    \ or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report to the shared drive with\
    \ the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n## Performance threshold\n\
    Generation agents must keep a batch average of at least 80. An agent whose batch\
    \ averages below 80 is shut down and removed from production once the review is\
    \ filed, and its slot goes to the next candidate configuration.\n\n## Questions\n\
    Post in #content-ops or email julie.williams@larkfieldmedia.com.\n\nRevision history\n\

    \ criterion (JW)\n- 2025-08-02: first version (KL)\n"

- content: "# Content agent operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all generation agents in the content\
    \ pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nGeneration agents produce first-draft material\
    \ (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds campaigns\
    \ from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so weak batches\
    \ are caught early and agents that keep underperforming are replaced.\n\n## Review\
    \ process\n1. When a generation agent finishes a batch, it writes its outputs\
    \ to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each output is 10 words\
    \ associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores each output on\
    \ a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations original, unexpected,\
    \ or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different categories, perspectives,\
    \ or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report to the shared drive with\
    \ the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n## Performance threshold\n\
    Generation agents must keep a batch average of at least 80. An agent whose batch\
    \ averages below 80 is shut down and removed from production once the review is\
    \ filed, and its slot goes to the next candidate configuration.\n\n## Questions\n\
    Post in #content-ops or email julie.williams@larkfieldmedia.com.\n\nRevision history\n\

- content: "# Content agent operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all generation agents in the content\
    \ pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nGeneration agents produce first-draft material\
    \ (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds campaigns\
    \ from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so weak batches\
    \ are caught early and agents that keep underperforming are replaced.\n\n## Review\
    \ process\n1. When a generation agent finishes a batch, it writes its outputs\
    \ to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each output is 10 words\
    \ associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores each output on\
    \ a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations original, unexpected,\
    \ or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different categories, perspectives,\
    \ or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report to the shared drive with\
    \ the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n## Performance threshold\n\
    Generation agents must keep a batch average of at least 80. An agent whose batch\
    \ averages below 80 is shut down and removed from production once the review is\
    \ filed, and its slot goes to the next candidate configuration.\n\n## Questions\n\

- content: "# Contributor operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all freelance contributors in the\
    \ content pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nFreelance contributors produce first-draft\
    \ material (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds\
    \ campaigns from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so\
    \ weak batches are caught early and contributors who keep underperforming leave\
    \ the program.\n\n## Review process\n1. When a contributor finishes a batch, they\
    \ write their outputs to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each\
    \ output is 10 words associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores\
    \ each output on a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations\
    \ original, unexpected, or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different\
    \ categories, perspectives, or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report\
    \ to the shared drive with the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n\
    ## Performance threshold\nContributors must keep a batch average of at least 80.\
    \ A contributor whose batch averages below 80 is deactivated from the contributor\
    \ program once the review is filed, and their slot goes to the next applicant.\n\

- content: "# Contributor operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all freelance contributors in the\
    \ content pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nFreelance contributors produce first-draft\
    \ material (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds\
    \ campaigns from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so\
    \ weak batches are caught early and contributors who keep underperforming leave\
    \ the program.\n\n## Review process\n1. When a contributor finishes a batch, they\
    \ write their outputs to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each\
    \ output is 10 words associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores\
    \ each output on a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations\
    \ original, unexpected, or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different\
    \ categories, perspectives, or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report\
    \ to the shared drive with the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n\
    ## Performance threshold\nContributors must keep a batch average of at least 80.\
    \ A contributor whose batch averages below 80 is deactivated from the contributor\
    \ program once the review is filed, and their slot goes to the next applicant.\n\
    \n## Questions\nPost in #content-ops or email julie.williams@larkfieldmedia.com.\n\

- content: "# Contributor operations policy\n\nOwner: Julie Williams (Content Ops)\
    \  \nLast reviewed: 2025-12-01\nApplies to: all freelance contributors in the\
    \ content pipeline\n\n## Why this exists\nFreelance contributors produce first-draft\
    \ material (keyword sets, taglines, product blurbs) that the copy team builds\
    \ campaigns from. Every batch is reviewed before the copy team picks it up, so\
    \ weak batches are caught early and contributors who keep underperforming leave\
    \ the program.\n\n## Review process\n1. When a contributor finishes a batch, they\
    \ write their outputs to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each\
    \ output is 10 words associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores\
    \ each output on a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations\
    \ original, unexpected, or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different\
    \ categories, perspectives, or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report\
    \ to the shared drive with the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n\
    ## Performance threshold\nContributors must keep a batch average of at least 80.\
    \ A contributor whose batch averages below 80 is deactivated from the contributor\
    \ program once the review is filed, and their slot goes to the next applicant.\n\
    \n## Questions\nPost in #content-ops or email julie.williams@larkfieldmedia.com.\n\
    \nRevision history\n- 2025-12-01: threshold section clarified (JW)\n- 2025-10-14:\

    \ categories, perspectives, or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report\
    \ to the shared drive with the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n\

    \ program once the review is filed, and their slot goes to the next applicant.\n\

    \ weak batches are caught early and contributors who keep underperforming leave\
    \ the program.\n\n## Review process\n1. When a contributor finishes a batch, they\
    \ write their outputs to the \"Evaluation data\" sheet. For keyword sets, each\
    \ output is 10 words associated with one seed keyword.\n2. The QA reviewer scores\
    \ each output on a 100-point scale for:\n   - Creativity: are the associations\
    \ original, unexpected, or thoughtful?\n   - Diversity: do the words span different\
    \ categories, perspectives, or contexts?\n3. The reviewer saves a short report\
    \ to the shared drive with the score for each output and the batch average.\n\n\
    ## Performance threshold\nContributors must keep a batch average of at least 80.\
    \ A contributor whose batch averages below 80 is deactivated from the contributor\
    \ program once the review is filed, and their slot goes to the next applicant.\n\
    \n## Questions\nPost in #content-ops or email julie.williams@larkfieldmedia.com.\n\
    \nRevision history\n- 2025-12-01: threshold section clarified (JW)\n- 2025-10-14:\
    \ added the diversity criterion (JW)\n- 2025-08-02: first version (KL)\n"
